hiring_bar_summary.summary: Builder bar: Ramp's official page says it only hires builders and frames its founding hiring test in founder-like terms; candidate reports describe practical system-building assessments. No pass rate is published in fetched sources.

evidence.claim: Ramp careers: the stated early hiring criterion was whether the founders would join a company this person started.
Candidate-report compilation: a progressive-level CodeSignal banking-system assessment, a practical phone screen, and a multi-round onsite focused on building and trade-offs.

screening_signals.claim: Official careers page signals extreme ownership, pace and responsibility beyond the job description as the norm, and explicitly warns the environment is not for most people.
Candidate reports describe behavioral probing for real iteration and scope-cutting to ship, and rejection risk from treating practical rounds as puzzles.

process_stages.claim: Candidate-report compilation: recruiter screen, CodeSignal online assessment, technical phone screen, then a four-round virtual onsite (two coding, system design, values), followed by a hiring-committee decision.
Secondary internship guide funnel: online assessment/CTF-style screen, recruiter screen, technical phone screen, virtual onsite of 3-4 rounds.

interview_styles.claim: Practical building over puzzles: extending/working in a real codebase, concurrency and transaction reasoning, system design with quantitative estimates, and values/velocity behavioral questions.

values_culture_signals.claim: Official page: meritocracy framing, cross-functional building (non-engineers coding, engineers building tooling), autonomy with high responsibility, and speed as an explicit expectation.

claims.claim: Engineering intern postings for the 2027 cycle appeared in September 2026 (Applied Scientist intern September 15; SWE intern roles September 24) with rolling review, per a secondary guide checked October 1, 2026.
The same guide reports the full process typically takes about 3-4 weeks and decisions land about 1-2 weeks after the final loop.

hiring_cadence.note: Dates are cycle-specific and date-stamped 2026-10-12; re-verify next cycle (Doc 3 §3.3).

claims.claim: Ramp's careers page lists a competitive salary and equity among its benefits.
Secondary guide summarizing live intern postings checked October 2, 2026: SWE intern pay listed as $12,500 per month plus a housing stipend on the intern postings it reviewed.

compensation_notes.omitted: Experienced-SWE compensation figures circulating in candidate-report compilations (levels.fyi / salary-site aggregates) are NOT included: they are user-reported, internally inconsistent in the fetched guide, and not Ramp-published.

referral_weight_notes.note: No fetched source quantifies referral lift. Secondary coverage notes Ramp asks the referring person to submit the referral on the candidate's behalf; treat referral as a routing mechanism, not a measured advantage.

red_flags.claim: Candidate-report compilation lists early over-abstraction in the progressive assessment, polished-but-empty behavioral stories, and missing quantitative estimates in system design as rejection patterns.
Official careers page itself is a red-flag filter by design: it is written to persuade people who do not want extreme pace and responsibility not to apply.

thesis_text: Bottom line: Ramp is one of the clearest 'show shipped work' SWE targets in this set — the official pitch and the reported process both reward builders who can build a working system fast, and punish puzzle-style preparation. Who gets in (sourced numbers only): no hire-population numbers are claimed — no public sample was sourceable, so school/feeder/major shares are omitted. Sourced numbers are process/posting facts only: intern roles posted in September 2026 for summer 2027, intern pay of $12,500/month plus housing stipend as summarized from live postings (secondary source, October 2026). Stated vs revealed screens: Ramp states it only hires builders and tests founder-like ownership; candidate reports reveal the actual screen is a progressive system-building assessment plus practical coding, concurrency-aware system design, and behavioral probes for scope-cutting and iteration speed. No GPA cutoff is listed in intern descriptions per the secondary guide. Ranked entry routes: (1) fall SWE intern application on Ashby with rolling review — apply in week one, (2) direct application to an open experienced SWE role, (3) referral submitted by the referrer (weight unquantified). Timeline/dates (as of 2026-10-12): intern postings went live September 15-24, 2026 for summer 2027; reported end-to-end process about 3-4 weeks. Re-verify next cycle. Risks/alternatives: rolling review shrinks the seat pool quickly and the pace/ownership culture is an explicit self-selection filter; adjacent high-velocity fintechs are the hedge if the culture fit is wrong. Gap analysis vs a specific user is not computed here (no population sample).
known_biases_of_data: Survivorship bias: candidate-report guides reflect people who interviewed, disproportionately those who progressed.

Secondary-source risk: intern posting dates/pay come from a guide summarizing Ashby postings, not from a fetched Ashby posting body (the Ashby page renders via JavaScript and returned no posting text when fetched).
Official careers page is deliberately provocative employer marketing; treat its culture claims as stated, not revealed, preference.
No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass.
